chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Al-A'ala ibn al-Fudayl, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When a man intends to strike another man unjustly, so the man defends himself or repels him from his own self, and causes him harm, then there is no compensation upon him.

key_terms.فَلَا شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ: there is nothing upon him (no compensation)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on causing harm to an attacker during self-defense?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith clarifies that self-defense against unjust aggression incurs no financial liability (diyah), emphasizing the principle of 'no harm' in Shia jurisprudence. It highlights that the defender is exempt from compensation even if the harm is significant, provided the initial aggression was unjust. This ruling underscores the right to preserve one's life and dignity without fear of retribution.
